question: Under RCW 18.85.111, what is the minimum age for an individual seeking a Washington managing broker's license?
choice_a: 25 years of age
choice_b: 18 years of age
choice_c: 19 years of age
choice_d: 21 years of age
explanation: RCW 18.85.111(1)(a) requires a managing broker applicant to be eighteen years of age or older, the same minimum age as for a broker's license.

question: Under the standard (non-alternate) experience pathway in RCW 18.85.111, how much full-time experience as a licensed real estate broker is required, and within what preceding period must it fall?
choice_a: Two years, within the preceding four years
choice_b: One year, within the preceding two years
choice_c: Three years, within the preceding five years
choice_d: Five years, within the preceding seven years
explanation: The standard pathway requires a minimum of three years as a full-time licensed real estate broker in Washington (or a comparable jurisdiction) within the preceding five years, or equivalent alternate experience as determined by rule.

question: How many total hours of approved real estate education must a managing broker applicant complete before sitting for the managing broker exam, under RCW 18.85.111(1)(d)?
choice_a: 90 hours
choice_b: 120 hours
choice_c: 60 hours
choice_d: 75 hours
explanation: A managing broker applicant must complete 90 hours of instruction, made up of three 30-hour courses in brokerage management, business management, and advanced real estate law.

question: The 90 hours of required managing broker coursework under RCW 18.85.111(1)(d) is broken into which three subject areas?
choice_a: Contract law, appraisal, and property management
choice_b: Ethics, marketing, and finance
choice_c: Fair housing, agency law, and escrow procedures
choice_d: Brokerage management, business management, and advanced real estate law
explanation: The department's managing broker license page and RCW 18.85.111(1)(d) both identify the three required 30-hour courses as brokerage management, business management, and advanced real estate law.
source_note: RCW 18.85.111(1)(d); DOL managing broker license page

question: Each of the three required managing broker courses under RCW 18.85.111(1)(d) must be at least how many clock hours, and completed within what time frame before the exam?
choice_a: At least 30 clock hours each, completed within 3 years before the exam
choice_b: At least 15 clock hours each, completed within 2 years before the exam
choice_c: At least 20 clock hours each, completed within 1 year before the exam
choice_d: At least 40 clock hours each, completed within 5 years before the exam
explanation: Each course must carry at least thirty clock hours of instruction and be completed within the three years immediately preceding the managing broker examination.

question: Under RCW 18.85.111(1)(d), besides completing the 90 hours of required coursework, what else must a managing broker applicant do with respect to each of the three required courses?
choice_a: Submit a letter of recommendation from their designated broker
choice_b: Pass the examination for each individual course
choice_c: Complete an unpaid internship at a supervising firm
choice_d: Nothing further is required beyond attendance
explanation: The applicant must pass the examination for each of the three required 30-hour courses, in addition to completing the instruction itself.

question: According to the Department of Licensing's managing broker page, which exams must a standard (non-reciprocity) managing broker applicant pass?
choice_a: No exam is required if the 90 hours of coursework is completed
choice_b: Only a state-specific managing broker exam
choice_c: Only a national real estate exam
choice_d: Both a national exam and a state exam
explanation: Standard applicants must pass both the national and state portions of the managing broker exam; only reciprocity applicants are limited to the state exam alone.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker

question: Under RCW 18.85.111(3), how many real estate firms may a single managing broker's license be affiliated with at any one time?
choice_a: An unlimited number of firms
choice_b: Up to two firms
choice_c: Up to three firms
choice_d: One firm only
explanation: RCW 18.85.111(3) provides that a managing broker can be licensed to one firm only at any one time.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, an applicant who has completed postsecondary education with a major study in real estate may substitute for the standard three-year broker experience requirement by combining that education with what?
choice_a: Six months of any real estate-related employment
choice_b: A separate appraisal license
choice_c: One year of experience as an actively licensed real estate broker in good standing
choice_d: Two years working as an unlicensed real estate assistant
explanation: One alternate qualification pathway pairs postsecondary education with a major study in real estate with at least one year of experience as an actively licensed real estate broker in good standing.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, a licensed attorney at law may qualify as an alternate pathway to the managing broker experience requirement with how much full-time real estate transactional practice?
choice_a: Not less than three years
choice_b: Not less than five years
choice_c: Not less than six months
choice_d: Not less than one year
explanation: A licensed attorney in good standing with at least one year of full-time practice involving real estate transactions may satisfy this alternate qualification pathway.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, how many years of full-time experience as a licensed mortgage broker or loan originator can substitute for the standard broker-experience requirement?
choice_a: Five years
choice_b: Ten years
choice_c: One year
choice_d: Two years
explanation: Five years of full-time experience in good standing as a licensed mortgage broker or loan originator is one of the alternate qualification pathways under WAC 308-124A-713.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, which of the following is listed as an acceptable alternate-qualification occupation, requiring five years of full-time experience in good standing, to substitute for the broker-experience requirement?
choice_a: A licensed home inspector
choice_b: A licensed limited practice officer or escrow agent
choice_c: A licensed general contractor
choice_d: A certified public accountant
explanation: Five years of full-time experience as a licensed limited practice officer or escrow agent, in good standing, is one of the recognized alternate qualification pathways.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, five years of full-time experience as a licensed or certified real property appraiser is treated the same way as which other alternate pathway, in terms of the years of experience required?
choice_a: The attorney pathway (which requires only one year)
choice_b: The mortgage broker/loan originator, escrow agent, and property management pathways (all requiring five years)
choice_c: No other pathway requires the same number of years
choice_d: The postsecondary-education-plus-broker-experience pathway (which requires only one year)
explanation: The appraiser, mortgage broker/loan originator, limited practice officer/escrow agent, and property management pathways all share the same five-year full-time experience requirement.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, an applicant with five years of full-time experience managing, leasing, selling, or buying real property may qualify under the alternate pathway only if that experience was performed on behalf of what?
choice_a: A federal government agency exclusively
choice_b: A nonprofit housing authority exclusively
choice_c: Their own personal residence only
choice_d: A third-party corporation, limited liability company, or partnership
explanation: The property management alternate pathway requires five years of full-time experience managing, leasing, selling, or buying real property on behalf of a third-party corporation, LLC, or partnership.

question: Under WAC 308-124A-713, within what time period before the application date must the alternate-qualification experience have been completed?
choice_a: There is no time limit
choice_b: Within 2 years before the application date
choice_c: Within 6 years before the application date
choice_d: Within 10 years before the application date
explanation: All alternate-qualification experience under WAC 308-124A-713 must have been completed within the six years immediately before the application date.

question: Under the Department of Licensing's reciprocity pathway for a managing broker license, an applicant's out-of-state license must have been active within what preceding period, and which exam must still be passed?
choice_a: Within the past 5 years; no exam required
choice_b: Within the past 6 months; only the state exam
choice_c: Within the past 2 years; only the national exam
choice_d: Within the past 30 days; both exams
explanation: A reciprocity applicant must have been actively licensed as a managing broker (or equivalent) in another state within the preceding 6 months, and needs to pass only the Washington state exam, not the national exam.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker

question: According to the Department of Licensing, an applicant qualifying through one of the alternate-qualification pathways (rather than the standard three-year broker experience) is given how many chances to pass both required exams?
choice_a: Three attempts
choice_b: One chance to pass both exams
choice_c: Five attempts within one year
choice_d: Unlimited attempts
explanation: Applicants who qualify through an alternate-qualification pathway are only given one chance to pass both the national and state exams, unlike standard applicants.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker

question: After passing the required exams, a managing broker applicant must complete what additional screening step, and how long do the results remain valid?
choice_a: A credit check, valid for 1 year
choice_b: A fingerprint background check, valid for 6 years from the date results are received
choice_c: A polygraph examination, valid indefinitely
choice_d: A driving record check, valid for 2 years
explanation: A fingerprint-based background check is required after passing the exams, and the results expire six years from the date they are received by the department.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker

question: According to the Department of Licensing, how long is a newly issued Washington managing broker license valid before it must be renewed?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 2 years
choice_c: 3 years
choice_d: 4 years
explanation: A managing broker license is valid for 2 years after it is issued, consistent with the general real estate license renewal cycle.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker

question: Reciprocity documentation submitted to support a managing broker license application must show license history from the other state including dates, licensure level, expiration, and disciplinary actions. According to the Department of Licensing, what form of documentation is NOT acceptable for this purpose?
choice_a: A certified printout from the other state's licensing database
choice_b: Photocopies or screenshots of the license itself
choice_c: A notarized letter from the issuing agency
choice_d: An official license history letter from the other state's regulator
explanation: The department requires official license history documentation from the other state; photocopies or screenshots of the license card itself are not sufficient.
source_note: DOL: Get your license - Real estate managing broker
